items.title: Sobolev traces and Gauss–Green formula on physical simplices

references.title: Jean-Luc Guermond, MATH 661 Fall 2025, Part VIII, Chapter 38: Discontinuous Galerkin
references.locator: §38.2.1, printed pp. 192–194: affine matching cells, face traces, and the elementwise Green identity used in SIP consistency.

references.title: Douglas N. Arnold, Franco Brezzi, Bernardo Cockburn, and L. Donatella Marini, Unified Analysis of Discontinuous Galerkin Methods for Elliptic Problems, SIAM Journal on Numerical Analysis 39(5) (2002)
references.locator: §§3.1–3.3, printed pp. 1756–1759: elementwise Sobolev traces, integration by parts, consistency, and adjoint consistency.

items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Let $d\ge2$, let $\widehat S_d$ be the reference simplex, and let $F_K(\widehat x)=b+B\widehat x$ map $\overline{\widehat S_d}$ affinely onto a nondegenerate closed simplex $K$, with $\det B>0$. Sobolev spaces on $K$ mean spaces on its open interior. For every scalar $u\in W^{1,2}(K)$ and vector field $G\in W^{1,2}(K;\mathbb R^d)$, each physical facet has bounded $L^2$ traces $\gamma_Fu$ and $\gamma_FG$, obtained by affine transfer from the reference trace maps. These traces are independent of the chosen orientation-preserving reference map, and they satisfy
$$\int_K u\,\operatorname{div}G+\nabla u\cdot G\,dx=\sum_{F\subset\partial K}\int_F(\gamma_Fu)(\gamma_FG)\cdot n_{K,F}\,dS,$$
where $n_{K,F}$ is the outward unit normal.

items.title: Symmetric interior-penalty DG form and energy seminorm

references.title: Jean-Luc Guermond, MATH 661 Fall 2025, Part VIII, Chapter 38: Discontinuous Galerkin
references.locator: §38.2.1–38.2.2, printed pp. 192–195: SIP bilinear form, gamma_0/h_F penalty, and broken energy norm.

references.title: Douglas N. Arnold, Franco Brezzi, Bernardo Cockburn, and L. Donatella Marini, Unified Analysis of Discontinuous Galerkin Methods for Elliptic Problems, SIAM Journal on Numerical Analysis 39(5) (2002)
references.locator: §§3.2–3.3, printed pp. 1757–1759: primal formulation, consistency, and adjoint consistency.

items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice for the Sobolev notation below. Each cell $K$ is the closed simplex from [[def-matching-affine-simplicial-meshes]]; in $W^{m,2}(K)$ notation, $K$ means its open interior, and its facets are the boundary faces of that interior. Write $H^m(K):=W^{m,2}(K;\mathbb R)$ for $m=1,2$. Use the mesh and jump convention of [[def-sipdg-jump-average-convention]]. Specialize [[def-broken-and-conforming-polynomial-spaces]] to scalar real polynomials of a fixed degree $k\ge1$, so $V_h^{\rm br}=\prod_{K\in\mathcal T}\mathbb P_k(K;\mathbb R)$. On every cell $K$, let $A_K\in\mathbb R^{d\times d}$ be a constant symmetric matrix. Assume common bounds $0<\lambda\le\Lambda<\infty$ such that
$$\lambda|\xi|^2\le \xi^TA_K\xi\le\Lambda|\xi|^2\qquad(\xi\in\mathbb R^d,\ K\in\mathcal T).$$
Write $A|_K=A_K$, let $h_F:=\operatorname{diam}(F)>0$, and fix a penalty parameter $\gamma>0$. Define $\mathcal D_h$ to consist of broken real-valued functions $v$ with $v|_K\in H^1(K)$, distributional $\operatorname{div}(A_K\nabla v|_K)\in L^2(K)$, and an $L^2(F)$ one-sided normal coefficient-flux trace $r_{K,F}(v)$ on every facet $F$ of each cell $K$. Precisely, $r_{K,F}(v)$ is the unique $L^2(F)$ function satisfying
$$\int_K A_K\nabla v\cdot\nabla\phi+\operatorname{div}(A_K\nabla v)\,\phi\,dx=\sum_{F\subset\partial K}\int_F r_{K,F}(v)\,\gamma_F\phi\,dS\qquad(\phi\in C^\infty(\overline K)).$$
Here $\gamma_F\phi$ is the value trace from [[lem-sipdg-physical-simplex-trace-green]]; uniqueness follows by testing smooth functions supported near the relative interior of each facet, whose restrictions are dense in $L^2(F)$. If $F=K^-\cap K^+$ and $n_F$ points outward from $K^-$, set $q_F(v):=\tfrac12(r_{K^-,F}(v)-r_{K^+,F}(v))$; on a boundary facet set $q_F(v):=r_{K,F}(v)$ with the outward normal. These definitions agree with $\{A\nabla_hv\}_F\cdot n_F$ whenever the classical one-sided vector flux traces exist. Broken polynomials and cellwise $H^2$ functions belong to $\mathcal D_h$ by [[lem-sipdg-physical-simplex-trace-green]]. For $v,w\in\mathcal D_h$, define
$$a_h(v,w):=\sum_{K\in\mathcal T}\int_K A_K\nabla v\cdot\nabla w\,dx-\sum_{F\in\mathcal F_h}\int_F q_F(v)[w]_F\,dS-\sum_{F\in\mathcal F_h}\int_F q_F(w)[v]_F\,dS+\gamma\sum_{F\in\mathcal F_h}h_F^{-1}\int_F[v]_F[w]_F\,dS,$$
All facet integrals and $L^2(F)$ norms use $(d-1)$-dimensional surface measure for the stated mesh dimension $d\ge2$. Counting measure is reserved for the separate one-dimensional interval examples in [[def-sipdg-jump-average-convention]]. The expression is real and symmetric.

Define the energy expression and its augmented version on $\mathcal D_h$ by
$$\|v\|_{DG}^2:=\sum_{K\in\mathcal T}\int_K A_K\nabla v\cdot\nabla v\,dx+\gamma\sum_{F\in\mathcal F_h}h_F^{-1}\|[v]_F\|_{L^2(F)}^2,$$
$$\|v\|_{DG,*}^2:=\|v\|_{DG}^2+\sum_{F\in\mathcal F_h}h_F\|q_F(v)\|_{L^2(F)}^2.$$
The first expression is initially a seminorm on $V_h^{\rm br}$; its definiteness is not part of this definition. The stated Sobolev notation follows [[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]]. Cellwise $H^2$ functions have the required value and normal coefficient-flux traces by [[lem-sipdg-physical-simplex-trace-green]], because $A_K$ is constant. The augmented expression is defined whenever $v\in\mathcal D_h$, so it applies in particular to the exact functions, dual functions and discrete polynomials used below.

For $f\in L^2(\Omega)$ define the discrete load $\ell_h(w):=\sum_{K\in\mathcal T}\int_K f w\,dx$. A symmetric interior-penalty DG solution is a function $u_h\in V_h^{\rm br}$ satisfying $a_h(u_h,w_h)=\ell_h(w_h)$ for every $w_h\in V_h^{\rm br}$.

items.title: Discrete inverse-trace bound for SIPDG coefficient fluxes

references.title: Jean-Luc Guermond, MATH 661 Fall 2025, Part VIII, Chapter 38: Discontinuous Galerkin
references.locator: §38.2.2, printed pp. 194–195: the discrete trace inequality used to bound the consistency flux.

references.title: Douglas N. Arnold, Franco Brezzi, Bernardo Cockburn, and L. Donatella Marini, Unified Analysis of Discontinuous Galerkin Methods for Elliptic Problems, SIAM Journal on Numerical Analysis 39(5) (2002)
references.locator: §4.1, printed pp. 1763–1764: inverse-trace control of the face consistency terms.

items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Let $\mathcal T$, $A_K$, $k$, $\lambda$, $\Lambda$, $h_F$, and $q_F$ be as in [[def-sipdg-bilinear-form-and-energy-norm]]. There is a constant $C_{\rm flux}<\infty$, depending only on $d$, $k$, $\sigma$, $\lambda$, and $\Lambda$, such that every $v_h\in V_h^{\rm br}$ satisfies
$$\sum_{F\in\mathcal F_h}h_F\|q_F(v_h)\|_{L^2(F)}^2\le C_{\rm flux}\sum_{K\in\mathcal T}\int_K A_K\nabla v_h\cdot\nabla v_h\,dx.$$
The constant is uniform over the mesh family and does not depend on its cell sizes. In particular, the penalty threshold derived from this estimate is mesh-degree and shape dependent; it is not a universal numerical constant.

items.title: The SIPDG broken energy expression is definite

references.title: Jean-Luc Guermond, MATH 661 Fall 2025, Part VIII, Chapter 38: Discontinuous Galerkin
references.locator: §38.2.2, printed p. 194: why the broken energy expression is a norm under weak homogeneous Dirichlet enforcement.

references.title: Douglas N. Arnold, Franco Brezzi, Bernardo Cockburn, and L. Donatella Marini, Unified Analysis of Discontinuous Galerkin Methods for Elliptic Problems, SIAM Journal on Numerical Analysis 39(5) (2002)
references.locator: §4.1, printed p. 1763: the mesh-dependent DG expressions are norms by the discrete Poincaré inequality.

items.statement: Assume Countable Choice. Let $\|\cdot\|_{DG}$ be the energy expression from [[def-sipdg-bilinear-form-and-energy-norm]] on a finite matching simplicial mesh of a nonempty bounded polyhedral domain, with $\lambda>0$ and $\gamma>0$. Then $\|\cdot\|_{DG}$ is a norm on $V_h^{\rm br}$.

items.title: Boundedness of the SIPDG form in the augmented norm

references.title: Jean-Luc Guermond, MATH 661 Fall 2025, Part VIII, Chapter 38: Discontinuous Galerkin
references.locator: §38.3, Lemma 38.9, printed pp. 197–198: face-aware boundedness of the SIP consistency terms.

references.title: Douglas N. Arnold, Franco Brezzi, Bernardo Cockburn, and L. Donatella Marini, Unified Analysis of Discontinuous Galerkin Methods for Elliptic Problems, SIAM Journal on Numerical Analysis 39(5) (2002)
references.locator: §4.1, printed pp. 1763–1764: boundedness of the primal DG form in the face-aware norm.

items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice and the SIPDG setting of [[def-sipdg-bilinear-form-and-energy-norm]], with $\gamma>0$. For all $v,w\in\mathcal D_h$,
$$|a_h(v,w)|\le C_B\|v\|_{DG,*}\|w\|_{DG,*},\qquad C_B:=2+2\gamma^{-1/2}.$$
The energy expression $\|\cdot\|_{DG}$ is also a seminorm on $\mathcal D_h$.

items.title: SIPDG adjoint consistency for piecewise H2 dual solutions

references.title: Jean-Luc Guermond, MATH 661 Fall 2025, Part VIII, Chapter 38: Discontinuous Galerkin
references.locator: §38.2.1 and §38.3, printed pp. 193 and 198–199: the symmetric adjoint-consistency term and its duality role.

references.locator: §3.3 and §5.1, printed pp. 1758–1759 and 1767–1768: the adjoint-consistency condition and its use in the L2 duality identity.

items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice and the mesh and coefficient hypotheses of [[def-sipdg-bilinear-form-and-energy-norm]]. Let $e|_K\in H^2(K)$ on every cell, and let $z|_K\in H^2(K)$ be a dual solution with matching interior traces, zero boundary trace, matching normal coefficient fluxes, and $-\nabla\cdot(A_K\nabla z)=e$ on every cell. Then the SIPDG form, extended to these piecewise regular functions by its same formula, satisfies
$$a_h(e,z)=\|e\|_{L^2(\Omega)}^2.$$

items.title: SIPDG coercivity above the discrete inverse-trace threshold

references.title: Jean-Luc Guermond, MATH 661 Fall 2025, Part VIII, Chapter 38: Discontinuous Galerkin
references.locator: §38.2.2, Lemma 38.6, printed pp. 194–195: inverse-trace threshold, coercivity, and well-posedness.

references.title: Douglas N. Arnold, Franco Brezzi, Bernardo Cockburn, and L. Donatella Marini, Unified Analysis of Discontinuous Galerkin Methods for Elliptic Problems, SIAM Journal on Numerical Analysis 39(5) (2002)
references.locator: §4.2, printed pp. 1765–1766: penalty terms absorb the consistency terms once the threshold exceeds the inverse-trace bound.

items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Use the mesh, coefficient field, energy norm, and form of [[def-sipdg-bilinear-form-and-energy-norm]], and let $C_{\rm flux}$ be the constant of [[lem-sipdg-discrete-flux-inverse-bound]]. If $\gamma\ge4C_{\rm flux}$, then
$$a_h(v_h,v_h)\ge\tfrac12\|v_h\|_{DG}^2\qquad(v_h\in V_h^{\rm br}).$$
Thus the discrete bilinear form is coercive with constant $1/2$ in the broken energy norm. For every $f\in L^2(\Omega)$, the finite-dimensional SIPDG system has a unique solution. The sufficient threshold depends on the polynomial degree, shape regularity, and coefficient ellipticity bounds; no universal penalty value is asserted.

items.title: SIPDG L2 error under adjoint consistency and dual approximation

references.title: Jean-Luc Guermond, MATH 661 Fall 2025, Part VIII, Chapter 38: Discontinuous Galerkin
references.locator: §38.3, Theorem 38.12 and its dual-problem setup, printed pp. 198–199: the s>1/2 regularity index and h^s ell_Omega^(1-s) L2 estimate.

references.title: Douglas N. Arnold, Franco Brezzi, Bernardo Cockburn, and L. Donatella Marini, Unified Analysis of Discontinuous Galerkin Methods for Elliptic Problems, SIAM Journal on Numerical Analysis 39(5) (2002)
references.locator: §5.1, printed pp. 1767–1768: adjoint consistency, Galerkin orthogonality, and duality for the L2 error.

items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice and the SIPDG setting of [[def-sipdg-bilinear-form-and-energy-norm]]. Let $u$ satisfy all hypotheses of [[thm-sipdg-exact-consistency]], and let $u_h\in V_h^{\rm br}$ satisfy $a_h(u_h,v_h)=\ell_h(v_h)$ for all $v_h\in V_h^{\rm br}$. Set $e:=u-u_h$, let $V:=H_0^1(\Omega;\mathbb R)=W_0^{1,2}(\Omega;\mathbb R)$ as in [[def-wkp-zero-as-a-sobolev-closure]], and let $h:=\max_{K\in\mathcal T}h_K$, with $0<h\le\ell_\Omega:=\operatorname{diam}(\Omega)$. Suppose $s\in(1/2,1]$ and a dual solution $z_e\in V$ exists satisfying
$$\sum_{K\in\mathcal T}\int_KA_K\nabla v\cdot\nabla z_e\,dx=\int_\Omega ve\,dx\qquad(v\in V),$$
with the following properties:

1. Its one-sided normal coefficient-flux traces are in $L^2(F)$ in the weak Green sense defining $\mathcal D_h$. In the branch $s=1$, assume also $z_e|_K\in H^2(K)$ on every cell, with matching interior value traces, zero boundary value trace, and matching interior normal coefficient fluxes; then [[lem-sipdg-adjoint-consistency-h2]] gives $a_h(e,z_e)=\|e\|_{L^2(\Omega)}^2$. In the branch $s<1$, assume this adjoint-consistency identity as an additional hypothesis. The weak dual equation gives $\operatorname{div}(A_K\nabla z_e)|_K=-e|_K\in L^2(K)$, so the stated flux and trace conditions place $z_e$ in the form domain $\mathcal D_h$ of [[def-sipdg-bilinear-form-and-energy-norm]].
2. The specified normed dual-regularity space $\mathcal R_s$ is a subspace of $V\cap\mathcal D_h$, and $\|z_e\|_{\mathcal R_s}\le C_{\rm reg}\|e\|_{L^2(\Omega)}$ for some $C_{\rm reg}\ge0$.
3. There is $z_h\in V_h^{\rm br}$ such that
$$\|z_e-z_h\|_{DG,*}\le C_{\rm app}h^s\ell_\Omega^{1-s}\|z_e\|_{\mathcal R_s}.$$
Here $C_{\rm app}\ge0$.

Then
$$\|e\|_{L^2(\Omega)}\le (2+2\gamma^{-1/2})C_{\rm app}C_{\rm reg}h^s\ell_\Omega^{1-s}\|e\|_{DG,*}.$$
The theorem retains the dual regularity exponent and the half-order face-flux contribution in $\|\cdot\|_{DG,*}$. It does not infer the dual approximation estimate or adjoint-consistency identity from elliptic regularity alone.

items.title: A direct Strang-type energy error estimate for SIPDG

references.title: Jean-Luc Guermond, MATH 661 Fall 2025, Part VIII, Chapter 38: Discontinuous Galerkin
references.locator: §38.3, Theorem 38.10, printed pp. 197–198: stability, consistency/boundedness, and the DG energy error estimate.

references.title: Douglas N. Arnold, Franco Brezzi, Bernardo Cockburn, and L. Donatella Marini, Unified Analysis of Discontinuous Galerkin Methods for Elliptic Problems, SIAM Journal on Numerical Analysis 39(5) (2002)
references.locator: §5.1, printed pp. 1767–1768: the stable, consistent DG energy estimate derived from coercivity, boundedness, and approximation.

items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice and the mesh, coefficient, penalty, and exact-solution hypotheses of [[thm-sipdg-exact-consistency]] and [[thm-sipdg-coercivity-large-penalty]]. Let $u_h\in V_h^{\rm br}$ be the unique discrete solution, so $a_h(u_h,v_h)=\ell_h(v_h)$ for every $v_h\in V_h^{\rm br}$. Let $C_{\rm flux}$ be the constant in [[lem-sipdg-discrete-flux-inverse-bound]] and put $C_B:=2+2\gamma^{-1/2}$. Then for every $w_h\in V_h^{\rm br}$,
$$\|u-u_h\|_{DG}\le\bigl(1+2C_B\sqrt{1+C_{\rm flux}}\bigr)\|u-w_h\|_{DG,*}.$$
Consequently $\|u-u_h\|_{DG}\le\bigl(1+2C_B\sqrt{1+C_{\rm flux}}\bigr)\inf_{w_h\in V_h^{\rm br}}\|u-w_h\|_{DG,*}$. The augmented approximation term retains the face-flux trace needed to bound the SIP consistency terms; no approximation rate is asserted without a separate bound on that term.

items.title: A broken polynomial with a nonzero jump is not globally H1
items.statement: On the interval partition $K^-=(0,1/2)$, $K^+=(1/2,1)$, let $v=1$ on $K^-$ and $v=0$ on $K^+$. This is a broken piecewise-constant polynomial with jump $[v]=1$ at the interior face. Its distributional derivative is a point mass, so $v\notin W^{1,2}(0,1)$.

items.title: One-dimensional SIPDG jump and penalty calculation
items.statement: This is a self-contained one-dimensional interval specialization of the jump convention in [[def-sipdg-jump-average-convention]]. Let $K^-=(0,1/2)$ and $K^+=(1/2,1)$, take unit coefficient, and set $h_F=1/2$ at the interior point face. Define $v(x)=x$ on $K^-$ and $v(x)=x-1$ on $K^+$. Then $v(0)=v(1)=0$, while the interior jump at $x=1/2$ is $1$ and the average derivative is $1$. The face contributions are $-\{v'\}[v]-\{v'\}[v]+\gamma h_F^{-1}[v]^2$. With penalty parameter $\gamma=1$, the bilinear form has value $a_h(v,v)=1$.

items.title: A too-small SIPDG penalty destroys coercivity
items.statement: Use the two-cell interval specialization and piecewise affine function described in **Given** below. At this mesh and with penalty $\gamma=1/4$, the function satisfies $a_h(v,v)=-1/2$. Hence the form is not coercive in this case, even though its energy expression on $v$ is positive.
